==English==
{{wp}}
[[File:Class in Colegio Preciosa Sangre, Pichilemu.jpg|thumb|A school '''class''']]

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:bor|frm:classe<ety:der<la:classis>>}}
From {{bor|en|frm|classe}}, from {{der|en|la|classis||a class or division of the people, assembly of people, the whole body of citizens called to arms, the army, the fleet, later a class or division in general}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*kelh₁-|t=to call, shout}}. {{doublet|en|clas|classis}}.

{{displaced|ang|ġecynd}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|kläs|a=RP,New England}}, {{IPA|en|/klɑːs/}}
* {{audio|en|en-uk-class.ogg|a=UK}}
* {{enPR|klăs|a=Northern England,Scotland}}, {{IPA|en|/klæs/|/klas/}}
* {{enPR|klăs|a=GenAm,NYC}}, {{IPA|en|/klæs/|/kleəs/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-class.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/klɑ(ː)s/|a=InE}}
* {{audio|en|En-class.ogg}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɑːs|æs|s=1}}
* {{hyphenation|en|class}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|countable}} A [[group]], [[collection]], [[category]] or [[set]] sharing [[characteristic]]s or [[attribute]]s.
#: {{ux|en|The new Ford Fiesta is set to be best in the 'small family' '''class'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|That is one '''class'''-A heifer you got there, sonny.}}
#: {{ux|en|Often used to imply membership of a large '''class'''.}}
#: {{ux|en|This word has a whole '''class''' of metaphoric extensions.}}
#* {{RQ:Plato Tredennick Socrates|page=21|passage=So I ask you to accept my statement that my critics fall into two '''classes''': on the one hand my immediate accusers, and on the other those earlier ones whom I have mentioned; {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=October 1, 2011|author=Saj Chowdhury|work=BBC Sport
|title=[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/15045306.stm Wolverhampton 1-2 Newcastle]
|passage=The Magpies are unbeaten and enjoying their best run since 1994, although few would have thought the '''class''' of 2011 would come close to emulating their ancestors.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q187588}} {{lb|en|sociology|countable}} A social grouping, based on [[job]], [[wealth]], etc. In Britain, society is commonly split into three main classes: [[upper class]], [[middle class]] and [[working class]].
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-28|author=w:Joris Luyendijk|volume=189|issue=3|page=21|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly|title=Our banks are out of control|titleurl=http://www.guardian.co.uk/commentisfree/joris-luyendijk-banking-blog/2013/jun/19/banking-britain-beyond-control|passage=Seeing the British establishment struggle with the financial sector is like watching an alcoholic{{...}}. Until 2008 there was denial over what finance had become. {{...}} But the scandals kept coming, and so we entered stage three – what therapists call "bargaining". A broad section of the political '''class''' now recognises the need for change but remains unable to see the necessity of a fundamental overhaul. Instead it offers fixes and patches.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013062852/https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/joris-luyendijk-banking-blog/2013/jun/19/banking-britain-beyond-control|archivedate=13 October 2026}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The [[division]] of [[society]] into classes.
#: {{ux|en|Jane Austen's works deal with '''class''' in 18th-century England.}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Admirable behavior; [[elegance]].
#: {{ant|en|vulgarity}}
#: {{ux|en|Apologizing for losing your temper, even though you were badly provoked, showed real '''class'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q18204}} {{lb|en|education|countable|and|uncountable}} A group of [[student]]s in a regularly scheduled meeting with a teacher.
#: {{ux|en|The '''class''' was noisy, but the teacher was able to get their attention with a story.}}
# A series of lessons covering a single subject.
#: {{ux|en|I took the cooking '''class''' for enjoyment, but I also learned a lot.}}
# A single lesson in a series.
#: {{ux|en|Tomorrow's '''class''' will cover long division.}}
# {{lb|en|countable}} A group of students who commenced or completed their education during a particular year. A [[school class]].
#: {{ux|en|The '''class''' of 1982 was particularly noteworthy.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1987|month=October|volume=172|number=4|title=Women of Saudi Arabia|author=Marianne Alireza|page=443
|text=Thirty years ago there were only a few high schools for boys, and in 1957 the first university '''class''' consisted of only 50 young men.}}
# {{lb|en|India}} a [[grade]], [[standard]], level of education.
# {{lb|en|countable}} A category of seats in an airplane, train or other means of mass transportation.
#: {{ux|en|I used to fly business '''class''', but now my company can only afford economy.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Andrew Martin|title=Underground Overground: A passenger's history of the Tube|publisher=Profile Books, {{ISBN|978-1846684777}}|page=101|text=The City & South London was also the first British passenger railway to offer only one '''class'''.}}
# {{senseid|en|Q37517}} {{lb|en|taxonomy|countable}} A [[rank]] in the classification of [[organism]]s, below [[phylum]] and above [[order]]; a [[taxon]] of that rank.
#: {{ux|en|Magnolias belong to the '''class''' Magnoliopsida.}}
# Best of its kind.
#: {{ux|en|It is the '''class''' of Italian bottled waters.}}
# {{lb|en|statistics}} A grouping of data values in an interval, often used for computation of a frequency distribution.
# {{senseid|en|Q217594}} {{lb|en|set theory}} A collection of [[set]]s definable by a shared property, especially one which is not itself a set (in which case the class is called [[proper class|proper]]).
#: {{ux|en|The '''class''' of all sets is not a set.}}
#: {{ux|en|Every set is a '''class''', but '''classes''' are not generally sets. A '''class''' that is not a set is called a proper '''class'''.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1973|author=w:Abraham Fraenkel; w:Yehoshua Bar-Hillel; w:Azriel Lévy|title=Foundations of Set Theory|edition=2nd|pageurl=https://books.google.com.au/books?id=ah2bwOwc06MC&pg=PA119&dq=%22class%22%7C%22classes%22+%22set+theory%22&hl=en&sa=X&ved=0ahUKEwiizv_k9pXcAhWIp5QKHV6lDvAQ6AEIVDAI#v=onepage&q=%22class%22%7C%22classes%22%20%22set%20theory%22&f=false|page=119|publisher=Elsevier
|passage=In the present section we shall discuss the various systems of set theory which admit, beside sets, also '''classes'''. '''Classes''' are like sets, except that they can be very comprehensive; an extreme example of a '''class''' is the '''class''' which contains all sets.{{...}}The main point which will, in our opinion, emerge from this analysis is that set theory with '''classes''' and set theory with sets only are not two separate theories; they are, essentially, different formulations of the same underlying theory.}}
# {{lb|en|military}} A group of people subject to be [[conscript]]ed in the same military [[draft]], or more narrowly those persons actually conscripted in a particular draft.
# {{senseid|en|Q4479242}} {{lb|en|object-oriented|countable}} A set of [[object]]s having the same [[behavior]] (but typically differing in [[state]]), ''or'' a [[template]] defining such a set in terms of its common [[property|properties]], [[function]]s, etc.
#: {{ux|en|an abstract base '''class'''}}
# One of the sections into which a [[Methodist]] [[church]] or [[congregation]] is divided, supervised by a ''class leader''.

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[assign]] to a class; to [[classify]].
#: {{ux|en|I would '''class''' this with most of the other mediocre works of the period.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=2|passage=She was a fat, round little woman, richly apparelled in velvet and lace, {{...}}; and the way she laughed, cackling like a hen, the way she talked to the waiters and the maid,{{nb...}}—all these unexpected phenomena impelled one to hysterical mirth, and made one '''class''' her with such immortally ludicrous types as Ally Sloper, the Widow Twankey, or Miss Moucher.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be grouped or classed.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1790|author=w:Edward Tatham|title=The Chart and Scale of Truth
|passage=the genus or family under which it '''classes'''}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To divide into classes, as students; to form into, or place in, a class or classes.
